The closures involve Seri Wawasan bridge, Seri Saujana bridge, Seri Gemilang bridge, Putra bridge and Seri Ehsan bridge, while Seri Bestari bridge and Seri Setia bridge will remain open.
Several other routes are also expected to be affected, including Lebuh Bestari, Lebuh Setia, Lebuh Saujana, Lebuh Gemilang, Lebuh Wawasan, Lebuh Sentosa, Jalan Tun Hussein, Persiaran Barat and Persiaran Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah.
“Members of the public are also encouraged to use the free shuttle bus services and obtain the latest information through the Putrajaya Corporation’s social media channels,” the infographic stated.
Meanwhile, in a video shared on the same platform, visitors were advised to prepare for hot weather by bringing an adequate supply of mineral water, sunglasses, umbrellas and hats, as well as face masks.
The 69th National Day celebration, themed ‘Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’, is scheduled to begin at 8 am, with more than 80,000 visitors expected to attend the historic celebration. — Bernama

Title: MB: Pahang strengthens mineral‑sector enforcement, orders probe after trailers suspected of moving minerals out of Raub site
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 30 — The Pahang government will step up enforcement against activities involving mineral resources to ensure that all such operations comply with the law.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government would also not compromise with any party that disregards the stipulated licence, permit and approval requirements.
“Enforcement will continue to be strengthened from time to time, including through the use of monitoring and intelligence technology, to ensure that the state’s mineral resources are managed in an orderly and responsible manner and in accordance with the law,” he said in a statement.
Wan Rosdy also said that he had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the transportation of minerals suspected to be iron ore in Raub yesterday.
He said intelligence efforts, including drone surveillance, detected three trailers suspected of transporting minerals out of the mining area before they were stopped for inspection by the Pahang Enforcement Unit (UPNP).
“We found that the drivers produced Form 13D and Delivery Orders (DOs) from approvals for other areas for the purpose of transporting the minerals,” he said.
Further inspection found that the mineral stockpile location indicated by the drivers was outside the permitted mining area specified in the documents produced.
“Enforcement personnel also found that the stockpile was located in an area with a temporary occupation licence, and all three drivers failed to produce valid documents or approvals relating to the location,” he said.
Following this, he said enforcement personnel detained the three drivers to assist in the investigation and seized three trailers believed to have been used to transport the minerals.
“The three individuals detained were taken to the Bentong district police headquarters (IPD) and subsequently released on police bail, while the three seized vehicles were taken to the UPNP Central Pahang Zone seizure site in Temerloh,” he said.
The seizures and arrests were carried out under Section 137 of the Pahang State Mineral Enactment 2001, while offences relating to information and breaches of terms or conditions are being investigated under Sections 159 and 165 of the same law. — Bernama

Title: Ahead of National Day, Anwar urges Malaysians to protect the nation and stay united
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the people to safeguard the country to the best of their ability and uphold unity as the pillar of Malaysia’s strength.
He said independence meant being free to determine one’s own destiny and having confidence in the strength of a dignified people and a sovereign nation.
“Uphold unity among Malaysians of various races as the pillar of our strength, and fill our independence with courage, confidence and a truly free spirit,” he said in a post on X today.
According to him, everything the people have achieved today came through the sacrifices of previous generations and was not attained easily.
“Everything we have achieved today came through the sweat, blood and tears of previous generations. Therefore, safeguard this country to the best of your ability,” he said.
In a video message also uploaded, Anwar said the Malay, Chinese, Indian, Iban, Kadazan, Murut, Bidayuh and Orang Ulu communities represented the strength of Malaysians.
He stressed that Malaysia’s interests must take precedence over ethnic and regional sentiments, while the country must be known as a nation that guarantees justice for all its people.
“Malaysia must be known for guaranteeing justice for all its people, including those who are marginalised and sidelined,” he said.
Anwar also urged the people to continue working as one team, preserve unity, boost their spirit and defend the country with all their might.
“This country gained independence through the collective strength of all Malaysians. Merdeka!” he said.
Malaysia will celebrate its 69th National Day tomorrow with the theme “Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati”. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: School maintenance allocation to rise from RM1b to RM1.5b in 2027
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The government will increase the maintenance allocation for all types of schools by 50 per cent, from RM1 billion to RM1.5 billion in 2027, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the additional allocation will cover all priority school streams, including national schools, Chinese and Tamil national-type schools, religious schools, tahfiz institutions, pondok schools, and special education.
“Everyone is guaranteed to receive additional allocations,” he said when delivering the National Day Prime Address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC), here today.
Anwar said the Ministry of Education (MOE) will also mobilise efforts to visit every district starting next month to examine every application for school infrastructure repairs.
He said this step is to ensure that infrastructure repair needs can be identified earlier and not delayed until next year.
Meanwhile, Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, also announced that the AI for the Rakyat Programme will be opened starting tomorrow (Sept 1), to 100,000 Malaysian youths aged 18 to 30.
Youths who complete the designated modules will receive a free three-month subscription to leading artificial intelligence (AI) applications.
“It includes local AI chat knowledge verified by the US-based local AI Gemini Enterprise, as well as Wonder Clip and Mul Run from China; everyone will get access starting tomorrow as soon as September 1,” he said.
For the public health sector, the Prime Minister said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will provide an allocation of RM1 billion to strengthen digital efficiency, including the implementation of an electronic medical records system and Internet connectivity in 150 hospitals and over 2,000 public health clinics.
He said the move aims to accelerate the treatment process, thereby reducing patient waiting times in public hospitals and health clinics.
Anwar said the government has also agreed to raise the e-Invoice implementation exemption threshold once again, from RM1 million to RM3 million per year, thereby exempting businesses with annual sales not exceeding RM3 million from the obligation to implement it.
Anwar also announced several immediate initiatives for the people, including an additional RM1 billion in micro-financing facilities, bringing the total fund for 2026 up from RM5 billion to RM6 billion.
The government will also introduce the Madani Prosperity Grant (Geran Sejahtera Madani) amounting to RM200 million to help hawkers, small traders, night market vendors, and mothers running home-based businesses.
Anwar said these announcements were made taking into account the cost of living pressures still faced by the public and cost pressures on micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), alongside needs related to school infrastructure and healthcare services.
He said although Budget 2027 will be tabled in the near future, several measures need to be implemented earlier because cost-of-living pressures and business requirements demand urgent action.
“Therefore, on the eve of independence, I am compelled to find a way, take steps, and announce something that can provide temporary relief to you, school children, youths, housewives, and mothers through today’s announcements,” he said.
The Prime Minister today announced six immediate initiatives for the people, covering students, youths, as well as small and medium-sized traders, all of which take effect starting Sept 1, 2026.
The six immediate initiatives include restoring the BUDI95 base eligibility from 200 to 300 liters per month; increasing the maintenance allocation for all types of schools for 2027 by 50 per cent, from RM1 billion to RM1.5 billion; and opening the AI Untuk Rakyat programme to Malaysian youths aged 18 to 30.
In addition, the immediate initiatives encompass the MCMC providing RM1 billion to strengthen the digital efficiency of the public health sector, covering the implementation of an Electronic Medical Records system and internet connectivity in 150 hospitals and over 2,000 public health clinics, as well as raising the e-Invoice exemption threshold once again from RM1 million to RM3 million per year.
The government will also add RM1 billion in micro-financing facilities, bringing the total fund for 2026 up from RM5 billion to RM6 billion, and introduce the RM200 million Madani Prosperity Grant. — Bernama

Title: Ferry operators urge urgent dredging of Kuala Kedah, Kuala Perlis lanes, warn silted routes could disrupt Langkawi schedules during peak season
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 30 — Langkawi ferry operators are appealing to the federal government to expedite dredging works in the shipping lanes in Kuala Kedah and Kuala Perlis which are now experiencing silt deposits that affect shipping safety.
Ferry Line Ventures Sdn Bhd operations manager, Lieutenant Commander (Retired) Norhafiz Abdul Wahid, said the increasingly shallow shipping lanes not only increase the risk to passenger ferry operations, but can also cause schedule disruptions and travel delays.
“Ferry services are the mainstay of transportation to Langkawi and play an important role in supporting the country’s tourism sector.
“Based on previous operational records, passenger ferry services are capable of transporting up to 25,000 tourists a day during peak season,” he said in a statement today.
According to him, if the dredging works are not carried out immediately, it is feared that the situation will affect the smooth operation of the ferry, especially during peak season including ahead of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) next year.
Norhafiz said comprehensive and periodic dredging works are needed to ensure that the shipping route is always safe, in addition to enabling ferry operations to run smoothly and accommodate the increase in passenger numbers.
In a related development, he announced that 176 regular ferry trips and 66 additional trips are scheduled between August 27 and September 6 to accommodate the school holiday season and National Day crowd.
He said about 90,000 passengers are expected travel via two main routes, namely Langkawi-Kuala Perlis-Langkawi and Langkawi-Kuala Kedah-Langkawi.
He added that so far 86,978 tickets have been sold through online sales, counters and reservations.
“Visitors are also advised to buy tickets in advance online via the Cuti-Cuti Langkawi application to avoid disappointment,” he said.
Norhafiz said his party would ensure that the level of readiness for ferry operations was at a high level throughout the school holiday season and National Day. — Bernama

Title: Anwar pledges billions in seized funds for health, education; eases rules for small businesses
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The government will channel billions of ringgit seized from illegal activities into public healthcare and education, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today, leading a series of fiscal announcements he said were aimed at supporting low-income groups and small businesses.
Speaking during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre here, Anwar said the move demonstrates the government's commitment to returning recovered proceeds of corruption and financial crime directly to the public.
"Today I declare that all funds seized from the proceeds of illegal activities through legal processes and decisions by the judiciary will be returned, especially for the people's education and healthcare," Anwar told the audience, including senior Cabinet ministers and top government officials who were also present.
As part of broader relief measures, Anwar also announced a new RM200 million grant scheme under the Geran Sejahtera Madani programme to assist hawkers, small traders, night market vendors, and mothers working from home.
The programme will take effect this coming Tuesday.
The government has also agreed to raise the mandatory e-invoicing exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million in annual sales, as part of reliefs to help the small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
The new threshold was among the list of measures Anwar said would provide "temporary relief" as his government aims to alleviate living cost pressure and help businesses.
Earlier the prime minister announced the monthly quota for petrol and diesel subsidies would be reverted to 300 and 400 litres respectively, a decision he said was initially intended to be unveiled as a Budget 2027 initiative.

Title: Amirudin says Pakatan prepared for all scenarios, including solo Melaka fight if BN deal fails
Article:
GOMBAK, Aug 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is always prepared for any eventuality in the Melaka state election, including contesting on its own should negotiations on cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN) fail to reach an agreement.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said, however, that sufficient room should be given to the party leadership to assess the best strategic options before any decision is finalised.
“There is still time, so let’s wait and see how things develop. I am not in a position to make the decision. So I have been asked to discuss it, and let’s discuss. But if there is no one to discuss with, what can we do? We just move forward,” he said when met by reporters after attending the National Aspirations with Youth (Nanba) for the Central Zone Series 2/2026 here today.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor Menteri Besar, said this when asked to comment on a previous statement by Melaka PKR state leadership council (MPN) acting chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim, who hinted at the possibility of PH contesting on its own should negotiations on cooperation with BN fail to reach an agreement.
He said the country’s political landscape remained dynamic and flexible, allowing each party room to determine its own approach in facing the election.
“As a political party, elections are our main business, and we will participate through various methods that can be considered.
“The situation is now rather fluid, and everyone can determine their own way of gaining the people’s support,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak Rivers Board warns Rajang journeys perilous as haze blinds boatmen, drought shrinks channels
Article:
SIBU, Aug 30 — River transport users in Sarawak have been advised to plan their journeys carefully and exercise greater vigilance amid the current drought and haze conditions to avoid untoward incidents.
Sarawak Rivers Board (LSS) chairman Dr Safiee Ahmad said the drought had caused river levels to fall, making navigation channels shallower and narrower, while haze had reduced visibility.
“Conditions become more challenging when haze causes limited visibility, especially at night. I advise all river transport users to plan their journeys as best as possible and, if possible, avoid travelling at night.
“In addition, reduce the speed of your respective boats or vessels as visibility is impaired due to haze, as river water levels are also falling due to the drought and lack of rain in upstream areas. This measure is crucial to prevent danger to other river users,” he told Bernama today.
Safiee, who is also the Daro state assemblyman, said LSS continuously monitored river conditions and carried out enforcement through its enforcement divisions at regional offices throughout Sarawak.
He said river transport users could also obtain the latest information on river water levels and advisory services from regional LSS offices to help them plan safe journeys.
A Bernama survey yesterday afternoon and today found thick haze blanketing the Rajang River, Malaysia’s longest river, as well as the Igan River, after API readings rose to unhealthy levels. — Bernama

Title: Debt dispute sparks armed George Town school fight, police arrest 13 suspects including minors
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 30 — Police have arrested 13 male suspects, including three minors, to assist in investigations into a violent brawl involving weapons that occurred in front of Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Kong Min branch in Air Itam here early yesterday.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said all the suspects, aged between 16 and 33, were arrested in five raids across the state through an operation conducted by the Criminal Investigation Department’s Vice, Gambling and Secret Societies Division (D7) of the Penang Police Headquarters, together with the Northeast District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Division and with assistance from the Central Police Station.
“All the suspects, including the three minors, were arrested under the joint operation, held from 8.19pm yesterday until 4.22am today, with those detained including a student, two unemployed individuals and several workers from the food delivery and transport sectors.
“Investigations are ongoing and the case is being probed under sections 148 and 326 of the Penal Code. The investigation papers will be completed before being referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further instructions,” he said in a statement today.
He said investigations found that the incident occurred at about 2.45am yesterday, with the armed brawl involving two primary targets aged 17 and 25, adding that it was believed to have stemmed from a debt dispute following a meeting between several individuals at a food court in Kota Bali, Paya Terubong here.
Lim said police were also investigating a vehicle that allegedly struck one of the victims during the brawl, inflicting injuries.
He said that as a preventive measure, police would step up patrols and monitoring at high-risk locations, enhance intelligence gathering and conduct targeted operations to curb group fights and violent crimes.
“Those with information regarding the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Insp Nurul Izzati Rohim at 013-4092884 or the nearest police station,” he added, while urging the public not to speculate or circulate the identities of the minors involved.
He also advised the public against taking the law into their own hands or resorting to violence to settle disputes.
Lim added that police would also consider action under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (SOSMA) if investigations found the offences met the requirements for its application. — Bernama

Title: Deputy minister presses Wisma Putra for hotline, briefings as 91 Malaysians missing in Nepal‑China
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Wisma Putra has been urged to establish a dedicated one-stop centre to provide direct, regular and consistent updates to the next of kin of 91 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the disaster at the Nepal-China border.
Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said the centre should be equipped with a 24-hour hotline, case reference numbers and officers who could be contacted at any time.
“A dedicated liaison officer must also be appointed for each family so that no next of kin is left out of the information loop and they do not have to contact various agencies to obtain updates,” he said in a statement today.
Based on a Wisma Putra statement as of 8pm yesterday, 55 Malaysians in Nepal and 36 in China remained uncontactable, with the figures still being verified and cross-checked to avoid duplicate reports.
Those uncontactable include tourists, climbers, pilgrims visiting Mount Kailash and two officers from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM).
Yuneswaran also proposed daily briefings at fixed times for the affected families, even if there was no new information.
“A silence of information will only add to the stress and suffering of the families,” he said.
He said coordination between Wisma Putra, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), JBPM, Nepalese and Chinese authorities, travel agencies and telecommunications companies must be intensified to verify travel manifests, passport numbers, travel routes and the last known locations of the individuals.
He also proposed that psychosocial support be provided to the families in collaboration with the Social Welfare Department and The Health Ministry, alongside assistance with documentation, travel and logistics for next of kin who need them.
He urged the public not to spread unverified information, photographs or figures, as this could cause confusion and heighten the families’ anxiety. — Bernama

Title: Budi95 quota restored to 300 litres, Anwar announces goodies ahead of Merdeka celebration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The monthly quota for petrol and diesel subsidies will be raised again, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim revealed today as he announced several goodies ahead of tomorrow’s Merdeka Day celebration.
Anwar suggested the move was initially intended to be unveiled as a Budget 2027 initiative, but he decided to announce it early as a means to provide “temporary relief”.
Currently the Budi95 programme sets the quota at 200 litres of subsidised RON95 a month. This will be raised back to 300 litres, effective 1 September 2026. For diesel, the quota would be raised from 300 to 400 litres a month. Anwar said the programme would benefit 16 million people.
The reversion to the original threshold is among a list of goodies the prime minister announced on the eve of Merdeka Day celebration here, where he delivered an official message that usually predates the National Day parade.
“It is hard but we must care for everyone. How do we ensure the T20 keep investing? How do we help the M40, the B40?” Anwar said, as he admitted to facing allegations that top and middle-income brackets often feel they are excluded from government programmes.
“With the M40, do we not give anything? I’d like to remind them that in 2023 we reduced income tax by 2 per cent. This led to the loss of RM1 billion in collection. Then there was the salary increment for civil servants. With school assistance, every family get it regardless of income background,” he added.
In his address, Anwar pointed to complaints that his government has not done enough, but suggested the accusations are ill-informed by highlighting all the major assistance that his leadership has provided up until now, including a staggering RM40 billion subsidy bill to keep petrol cheap even for high income earners.
“There is a tendency to complain about what the government has not yet done, but never to admit to God and be grateful for what we have received,” he said.
“I’ll give you an example, there is assistance that cost RM40 billion for all. What is that? Budi95.”
Anwar’s coalition secured the most seats at the 15th general election on the promise to alleviate cost of living pressure.
Despite strong growth numbers, among them a 6 per cent growth recorded in the April to June period, there is still grumbling that much of that prosperity is not trickling down, a point the prime minister acknowledged in his speech.
“Even in these tough times, we raised the SARA cash assistance, for example to RM15 billion, the highest in history. Is this the solution to all, no. Will this solve the living cost pressure, not yet,” he said.
“We admit that there are still steps to be taken.”

Title: Melaka’s Ab Rauf to steer BN–Pakatan talks, Zahid says timing depends on dissolution
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 30 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi says formal negotiations with Pakatan Harapan (PH) on possible cooperation for the Melaka state election will begin only after the state assembly is dissolved.
He confirmed the matter but explained that the talks would be led by Melaka BN under Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who has been tasked with negotiating and finalising any decisions,
Berita Harian
(BH) reported today.
The deputy prime minister, who is also Umno president, noted that only informal discussions between BN and PH have taken place so far.
He said Ab Rauf had already briefed the BN political bureau in Melaka, with details presented to the party’s supreme council for further study based on data compiled by its war room.
“We are handing this to Datuk Seri Ab Rauf, and I believe he will hold formal discussions once the Melaka assembly is dissolved,” Zahid told BH.
Separately, PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the coalition was waiting for Ab Rauf to indicate his readiness before negotiations could begin.
The PKR vice president, who is leading the talks, added that he had contacted Ab Rauf but was told to wait for a policy decision from BN and Umno’s central leadership.
